quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It blocks your side vision.
It can reduce how bad a head injury is.
It is usually uncomfortable.
It makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can reduce how bad a head injury is.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Every time you change lanes.
Only when it is dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a crash?

options.text: Experienced riders.
New riders.
Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who took a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: New riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with untrained, new riders who don't know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: Your friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use quiet roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: What is true about clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
It should not cover your arms and legs completely.
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather.
It can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly but not restrict movement.

questions.question: Why should you rise off your seat when riding over bumps or potholes?

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you.
So you can see the bumps better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When you rise off your seat, your joints absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is true about checking mirrors while riding?

options.text: They should be part of your regular checking routine.
You should avoid them because they distract you.
You should avoid them because other drivers can see you.
You should only check them in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be part of your regular checking routine.
questions.explanation: For safety, know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider slow down?

options.text: Downshifting.
Upshifting.
Cross-shifting.
Rolling on the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: Riders often slow down by downshifting. Know that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding your motorcycle, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drunk riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: On average, your body removes one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can still affect your riding ability.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. These include wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers. Dry pavement is safest for motorcyclists.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they usually won't affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, they are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Always learn the side effects of any drug before riding.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Assume they have ridden on a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
Do not let them ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: A passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Never assume they know what to do. Give clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take and how often should you do it?

options.text: A few minutes and once a month
A few minutes and before every ride
Over an hour and only by a mechanic
Over an hour and only if carrying a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and before every ride
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It should take only a few minutes.

questions.question: When your turn is obvious, do you still need to use a turn signal?

options.text: No, you do not need to use a turn signal.
Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
Only if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if it seems obvious. Other vehicles may not see you or may not have noticed you yet.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Only the front brake
Only the rear brake
Both brakes at the same time
One brake, never both together

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together to stop. They work best when used at the same time.

questions.question: What is the rule for passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can ride on the shoulder.
You can pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk to get them to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must be done within posted speed limits and only in safe, legal areas.

questions.question: What kind of shoe soles should motorcycle riders wear?

options.text: Hard, tough, and slip-resistant
Light material that lets feet breathe
Tall heels
Soft, flimsy material

questions.correctAnswerText: Hard, tough, and slip-resistant
questions.explanation: Wear riding boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to protect your ankles. Choose footwear with soles made of hard, tough, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you adjust your riding?

options.text: Ride faster than usual
Ride more slowly than usual
Start slowing later than usual
Try to squeeze into smaller traffic gaps

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. It will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride more slowly, slow down sooner, keep a bigger space cushion, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: What type of sign is usually rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should continually scan the road ahead for:

options.text: Road conditions.
Traffic conditions.
Escape routes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Keep watching the road ahead. Look for changing traffic, bad road conditions, and ways to escape danger. Be ready to react quickly to anything that changes.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Are unimportant.
Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular riding habit. Also check mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When you ride, the best gear to wear is:

options.text: Any gear that helps to protect you.
The lowest-priced gear.
Gear that looks good.
Any gear that fits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps to protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects your body. The best choice is a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces does not provide poor traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces can be dangerous for motorcycle tires. Wet roads, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all more hazardous than dry pavement.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while you are riding.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.
Should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good protection means your jacket and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. Your clothes should fit snugly but be loose enough to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection if you crash.
